newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan February M2 money supply up 9.88 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan February M2 money supply up 9.88 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2, grew 9.88 percent in February compared to February 1996, the central bank said on Tuesday.

February was the second month in which the central bank used a revised definition of M2 measure. Analysts have said the new broader definition could be expected to add 1.0 to 1.5 percentage points to the figure.
The year-on-year February M2 increase fell somewhat short of an average forecast of 10.07 percent compiled from a March 21 Reuters Poll of Taiwan economists.
The central bank attributed the M2 growth mainly to active stock trading and a decline in governemnt deposits.
The year-on-year increase put M2 growth within the central bank's target zone of 9-14 percent growth for the second consecutive month.
January's M2 money supply growth was 9.35 percent year-on-year.
Economists have noted slowly increasing money demand, although most of the money flooded into a stock market that had seen dramatic rises until one week ago.
The central bank said it revised its definition of M2 to reflect Taiwan's liberalising financial infrastructure.
According to the central bank's previous definition, M1A was cash, checking accounts and passbook deposits. M1B was M1A plus savings accounts. M2 was M1B plus quasi-money.

Under the revision, the central bank said it was retaining its M1A and M1B definitions, but redefining M2 as M1B plus time deposits, foreign currency deposits, postal funds, repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings.

The new M2 definition uses the post offices' total deposits instead of their redeposits in banks, adds repurchase agreement trade outstanding and foreigners' Taiwan dollar holdings, and deletes the net value of financial bonds, savings bonds and treasury bills and foreign-currency trust funds.
